title: Lyft Scales Global Localization Using AI and Human-in-the-Loop Review
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/lyft-ai-localization-pipeline/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775411926263.jpg"/><p>Lyft has implemented an AI-driven localization system to accelerate translations of its app and web content. Using a dual-path pipeline with large language models and human review, the system processes most content in minutes, improves international release speed, ensures brand consistency, and handles complex cases like regional idioms and legal messaging efficiently.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: Reimagining Platform Engagement with Graph Neural Networks
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/graph-neural-networks/en/mediumimage/Mariia-Bulycheva-medium-1775048997053.jpeg"/><p>Mariia Bulycheva discusses the transition from classic deep learning to GNNs for Zalando's landing page. She explains the complexities of converting user logs into heterogeneous graphs, the "message passing" training process, and the technical pitfalls of graph data leakage. She shares how a hybrid architecture solved inference latency, delivering contextual embeddings to a downstream model.</p> <i>By Mariia Bulycheva</i>

title: Article: The Spring Team on Spring Framework 7 and Spring Boot 4
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/spring-team-spring-7-boot-4/en/headerimage/spring-team-spring-7-boot-4-header-1775634533622.jpg"/><p>InfoQ recently spoke with key members of the Spring team about the significant architectural and functional advancements in Spring Framework 7 and Spring Boot 4. This conversation explores the strategic shift toward core resilience by integrating features such as retry and concurrency throttling directly into the framework, alongside the performance benefits of modularizing auto-configurations.</p> <i>By Karsten Silz, Phil Webb, Sam Brannen, Rossen Stoyanchev, Mark Pollack, Martin Lippert, Michael Minella</i>

title: Podcast: How SBOMs and Engineering Discipline Can Help You Avoid Trivy’s Compromise
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/help-avoid-trivy-compromise/en/smallimage/the-infoq-podcast-logo-thumbnail-1775549272964.jpg"/><p>Viktor Peterson, part of the CISA task force working on SBOM blueprints and co-founder of sbomify, explores the shifting landscape of software supply chain security as the EU's Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) comes into force, a "GDPR moment" for the industry.</p> <i>By Viktor Peterson</i>

title: AWS Launches Sustainability Console with API Access and Scope 1-3 Emissions Reporting
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS launched a standalone Sustainability console with API access, configurable CSV exports, and Scope 1-3 emissions data by service and Region. The console decouples emissions reporting from billing permissions. AWS CTO Werner Vogels framed carbon as an architectural metric belonging alongside latency, cost, and error rates in the observability stack.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Anthropic Releases Claude Mythos Preview with Cybersecurity Capabilities but Withholds Public Access
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/anthropic-claude-mythos/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775828239509.jpg"/><p>Anthropic has introduced Claude Mythos Preview, its most advanced AI model, improving significantly in reasoning, coding, and cybersecurity. Unlike previous releases, it will not be publicly available. Access is limited to a consortium of tech companies through Project Glasswing. Internal tests revealed the model's ability to discover critical security flaws effectively.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Java News Roundup: JDK 27 Release Schedule, Hibernate, LangChain4j, Keycloak, Helidon, Junie CLI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/java-news-roundup-apr06-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1776028062977.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for April 6th, 2026, features news highlighting: the fifth preview of Primitive Types in Patterns, instanceof and switch; the proposed release schedule for JDK 27; point releases of Hibernate, LangChain4j, Keycloak and Google ADK for Java; a maintenance release of Helidon; a CVE in Spring Cloud Gateway; and the Junie CLI integrated in JetBrains IDEs.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: GitHub Copilot CLI Reaches General Availability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/github-copilot-cli-ga/en/headerimage/header-1775595985599.jpeg"/><p>GitHub has launched Copilot CLI into general availability, bringing generative AI directly to the terminal. Integrated with the GitHub CLI, it offers natural language command suggestions and code explanations. Recent updates introduce "agentic" workflows with Autopilot mode and GPT-5.4 support, alongside new enterprise telemetry for tracking usage across development teams.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Etsy Migrates 1000-Shard, 425 TB MySQL Sharding Architecture to Vitess
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/etsy-vitess-sharding-migration/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1774855136721.jpg"/><p>The Etsy engineering team recently described how the company migrated its long-running MySQL sharding infrastructure to Vitess. The transition moved shard routing from Etsy’s internal systems to Vitess using vindexes, enabling capabilities such as resharding data and sharding previously unsharded tables.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Presentation: Latency: the Race to Zero...Are We There Yet?
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/latency-techniques/en/mediumimage/amir-langer-medium-1774444318217.jpg"/><p>Amir Langer discusses the evolution of latency reduction, from the Pony Express to modern hardware. He explains how separation of concerns - decoupling business logic from I/O - and tools like Aeron and the Disruptor achieve single-digit microsecond speeds. He shares insights into replicated state machines, consensus protocols like Raft, and the future of low-latency sequencer architectures.</p> <i>By Amir Langer</i>

title: CNCF and Kusari Partner to Strengthen Software Supply Chain Security across Cloud-Native Projects
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/cncf-kusari-security/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775306473905.jpg"/><p>The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Kusari have announced a new collaboration aimed at strengthening software supply chain security across cloud-native projects, providing free access to Kusari's AI-powered security tooling for CNCF-hosted projects.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Google Cloud Highlights Ongoing Work on PostgreSQL Core Capabilities
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/google-cloud-postgresql/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775811962259.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has outlined its recent technical contributions to PostgreSQL, emphasizing improvements in logical replication, upgrade processes, and overall system stability. The update reflects ongoing collaboration with the upstream community and focuses on enhancements to the core engine aimed at addressing scalability, replication, and operational challenges.</p> <i>By Robert Krzaczyński</i>

title: Safari Adds Scrollend Event Support, Completing Baseline Browser Coverage
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/safari-scrollend-support/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775736557972.jpg"/><p>Safari's release of version 26.2 in December introduced support for the scrollend event, completing its alignment with major browsers. This event signals when scrolling has definitively ended, enabling more reliable interactions without the need for workarounds. It improves performance for developers managing UI updates and data fetching based on scroll completion.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Podcast: Tiger Teams, Evals and Agents: The New AI Engineering Playbook
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/tiger-teams-evals-agents/en/smallimage/engineering-culture-podcast-thumbnail-1775220077178.jpg"/><p>In this podcast Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods spoke to Sam Bhagwat, co-founder and CEO of Mastra, about building and sustaining open source communities, the emerging discipline of AI engineering and evals, and how cross-functional Tiger Teams are key to shipping agentic applications.</p> <i>By Sam Bhagwat</i>

title: Cloudflare Introduces EmDash: TypeScript CMS Positioned as WordPress Successor
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/04/cloudflare-emdash-wordpress/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1775658833509.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently announced the preview of EmDash, a new open-source CMS it describes as a “spiritual successor to WordPress.” Designed to rebuild the CMS model around a serverless, developer-focused architecture, EmDash includes AI-native features, developer tooling, and migration paths from WordPress, sparking debate across the WordPress and broader CMS community.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>
